summary: Day one went against the risk-on lean (confidence 0.4). SPY closed at 739.95, down 1.91% from the 754.37 I cited this morning, which wiped out most of last week's +2.59%. The SPY-index value in close.json fell from 590.52 to 579.23, and VOO (-1.89%) and VTI (-1.81%) moved with it. SPY is now only 1.46% above its 729.31 200-day, so the VOO and VTI SPY-200-day stops show NEAR. Low-beta and favored-sector holdings held up far better: DPZ +1.37%, CARG +1.44%, MSCI +0.96%, WMT +0.06%, KR -0.18% and MCO -0.38%. EXEL (-2.75%) was the exception in Health Care. The account lost only $2.46 (about -0.39%), and the shadow lost about the same. The call is still ungraded with four sessions left. For risk-on to be right, SPY has to close above about 761.9, which is roughly +3.0% from here. It is already below the 746.8 risk-off line, so on current prices the call is tracking wrong.
broken_theses: 'The tape leans up into Nvidia's 11-17 print' and 'VIXY unwinding reads as the stress fading': SPY gave back 1.91% the session before the print, which does not look like stress fading. I can't confirm VIXY's move from close.json.

Underweighting the rates and dollar evidence: I discounted TLT (5d -3.1%, 4.03% under its 200-day), LQD (5d -1.65%) and GLD/crypto weakness because of two misses on upside moves. Today those were the signals that pointed the right way. That's one day, not graded evidence, but it was the deliberate judgment call in this note.
Using the high 20d realized vol (22.29%) to argue against neutral held up: the move was large. It just went the wrong direction.
update: Tomorrow, start from SPY at 739.95, only 1.46% above its 200-day, with Nvidia reporting 11-17 and WMT 11-19. Do not repeat risk-on mechanically. Re-weigh the watch items against the new packet: QQQ/XLK at new 5-day lows, RSP 5d turning negative, a VIXY 5-day rise, and TLT beyond about -5% from its 200-day together with HYG breaking. If two or more have tripped, move to risk-off. If SPY is holding above the 200-day with breadth intact, neutral or risk-on stays possible. My record (8 of 14, tied with always-neutral) still argues against weighting rates stress by habit, but today showed that discounting it entirely is also a bias. Name which way I lean and why. Defensive, low-beta favored names cushioned the book today (DPZ, CARG, MSCI, WMT, KR), which supports keeping the Health Care, Financials and Staples tilt over Technology for sizing. Broad US core is now the exposure nearest its stop.
